title: August and the Inheritance
premise: Estate lawyer Yara Marchetti, who has quietly solved three deaths the police ruled accidental, is hired by a nervous client to prove a murder that hasn't happened yet: his sister's death at the family's anniversary dinner. Digging into the Halvorsen estate, Yara finds a will dated after the client's own supposed signature and a case file annotated in handwriting she recognizes — her own. The killer is someone who has studied her methods and plans to frame her for the murder she was hired to prevent. At the anniversary dinner, Yara swaps the poisoned toast, forces a confession on record, and chooses to hand the evidence not to the police but to the victim's daughter, keeping justice outside the law one last time.
about_author: N. M. Ashgrove spent a decade working in probate offices before turning to fiction, where the paperwork of grief became an endless source of stories. They write from a coastal town where fog rolls in early and everyone's will has at least one strange clause.

chapters.title: The Will That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Yara Marchetti's POV. A retainer arrives with payment in full for a murder that hasn't occurred — the client's sister, due to die at the Halvorsen anniversary dinner in nine days. Reviewing the estate file, Yara finds a codicil signed with her own forged initials. The beat is cold dread: for the first time, the invisible solver is inside someone else's plan.

chapters.title: Nine Days of Paperwork
chapters.summary: Alternating Yara and the client, Elias Halvorsen. Yara interviews the household under pretext of estate planning while Elias grows erratic, insisting he never sent the retainer. She discovers the case file contains details only the killer could know — including her three solved deaths. The emotional beat shifts from suspicion of Elias to the vertigo of being hunted through her own methods.

chapters.title: Anniversary Glass
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, dinner night. She attends as 'estate counsel,' swaps the toast glasses, and watches the killer improvise when the poison fails — revealing herself deliberately to force a private confrontation in the wine cellar. The killer confesses the pattern: each victim had wronged them, each death staged as accident, each file left open like a calling card. Climax: Yara records it all, then the cellar door locks from outside.

chapters.title: Probate
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, aftermath. Escaped and unharmed, she faces the choice she's always avoided: police, or something quieter. She gives the recording to the victim's daughter, lets the family bury its scandal privately, and burns the forged codicil — but keeps one page as insurance against whoever wrote it. The final beat is bittersweet resolve: invisibility was always a story she told herself.
